name: PixiTween Director S07a: Clippy client, approval gate, request builder, mode and approve routes, panel
description: The first half of generate mode: a typed, tested Clippy MCP client; the single-use approval tokens and the guard that makes animate_image unreachable without one; the request builder (10 s rule, prompt limits, idempotency keys); the scene source still; the public-URL rule; the mode and approve routes with a runner registry (S7b plugs in the runner); and the approval panel. Offline only: no Clippy or Meta call in any story. Leaves out: polling, download, swap-in, clip check (S7b).

userStories.title: Clippy MCP types: zod schemas and constants
userStories.description: As a server developer, I want typed, validated shapes for the Clippy MCP tools so that bad requests are caught before any credit is reserved.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md section 4.1 (the verified animate_image contract, result shapes and server-side validation rules) and shared/tools.ts for the zod conventions.

Create server/clippy/types.ts exporting constants CLIPPY_ESTIMATED_CREDITS = 25, FAST_H3_MIN_SEC = 5.2, MAX_CLIP_SEC = 10, FAST_H3_PROMPT_MAX = 800, OMNI_PROMPT_MAX = 8000, OMNI_SECONDS = [5.875, 8, 10.125, 12.25, 14.375] as const.

In the same file export zod schemas and inferred types: animateImageArgsSchema (a discriminated union on `model`: 'fast-h3' requires an https sourceImageUrl, prompt <= 800, durationSec 5.2-14.375, aspect '16:9'|'9:16'|'1:1', no imageUrls with more than one entry; 'fast-h3-omni' requires imageUrls 1-9 https, prompt <= 8000, durationSec exactly one of OMNI_SECONDS (tolerance 1e-6), aspect '16:9'|'1:1'|'9:16'|'4:3'; both take an optional idempotencyKey matching /^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{8,200}$/), submitResultSchema { jobId, status, estimatedCredits }, statusResultSchema { jobId, status: 'queued'|'planning'|'rendering'|'done'|'failed'|'cancelled', progress?, resultUrl: string | null, resultUrlExpiresAt?: string | null, error?: unknown, creditsCharged?: number } and balanceResultSchema { currentBalance: number } (the last two use .passthrough() so unknown fields survive).
Create hand-authored fixtures fixtures/s07a/submit-result.json, status-done.json, status-rendering.json and balance.json, each containing "_handAuthored": true, shaped as in the design section 4.1.
Create server/clippy/types.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: animateImageArgsSchema accepts { model: 'fast-h3', prompt: 'x', sourceImageUrl: 'https://a.example/i.jpg', durationSec: 5.2, aspect: '16:9' } and rejects the same with an http:// URL, with an 801-character prompt, with durationSec 5.1, and with imageUrls of two entries
The omni variant accepts durationSec 8 and 5.875 and rejects 10 and 9.99; it accepts 1 to 9 imageUrls and rejects 10
The four fixtures parse with their schemas (the _handAuthored key does not break parsing) and statusResultSchema rejects status 'unknown'
idempotencyKey 'film1:s2:1' parses; 'short' and 'has space in it' are rejected
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Clippy MCP client over Streamable HTTP
userStories.description: As a server developer, I want a typed client for Clippy's MCP server so that generate mode can read balances and submit jobs.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 4.1 and 11 (SDK facts), server/clippy/types.ts, and the installed SDK typings in node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/index.d.ts and streamableHttp.d.ts (confirm Client, StreamableHTTPClientTransport, requestInit, callTool, terminateSession) and its server side (server/mcp.js, server/streamableHttp.js) for the test server.

Create server/clippy/mcp.ts exporting interface ClippyClient { listLiveAnimateModels(): Promise<unknown>; getCreditBalance(): Promise<BalanceResult>; animateImage(args: AnimateImageArgs): Promise<SubmitResult>; getLiveAnimateStatus(jobId: string): Promise<StatusResult>; cancelLiveAnimate(jobId: string): Promise<unknown>; close(): Promise<void> }, class ClippyError extends Error { tool: string; isToolError: boolean; status?: number } and createClippyClient({ url, token, timeoutMs = 60000 }): ClippyClient.

Implementation: lazy connect on first use with `new Client({ name: 'pixitween-director', version: '1' })` and `new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL(url), { requestInit: { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } } })` (imports from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js' and '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/streamableHttp.js'); each method uses client.callTool({ name, arguments }); an MCP result with isError becomes ClippyError carrying the server's text; otherwise parse the first text content item as JSON and validate it with the matching zod schema (ClippyError('unexpected response') on failure). The token never appears in any error message (replace it with '[redacted]').

Create server/clippy/mcp.test.ts that starts a node:http server on port 0 hosting an SDK McpServer over StreamableHTTPServerTransport (stateless) with tools get_credit_balance, animate_image and get_live_animate_status returning JSON text content, and records the Authorization header it sees.
If the wildcard subpath import does not resolve under the repository's moduleResolution, fix the import path or tsconfig setting minimally and record what was needed in notes.
acceptanceCriteria: getCreditBalance() against the test server returns an object with currentBalance equal to the number the test server returns, and the server saw the header 'Bearer test-token'
A tool result with isError true makes the client method reject with ClippyError whose message contains the tool name and the server text and does not contain 'test-token'
A tool result whose text is not valid JSON rejects with ClippyError 'unexpected response'
close() ends without error and `npm run typecheck` passes with the two SDK imports
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Client timeouts and read-only retries
userStories.description: As a server developer, I want reads to retry once and writes never to retry so that a flaky network cannot double-charge a clip.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md section 7 (errors table) and server/clippy/mcp.ts.

In server/clippy/mcp.ts add a per-call timeout (timeoutMs, default 60000; ClippyError('timeout') when exceeded) and `withReadRetry` used by listLiveAnimateModels, getCreditBalance and getLiveAnimateStatus: on a transport error (not a tool error) retry once after 2000 ms via an injectable `sleep`.
animateImage and cancelLiveAnimate are never retried automatically.
Extend server/clippy/mcp.test.ts: a test server that fails the first status request at the HTTP level and succeeds the second; a test server that never answers.
acceptanceCriteria: A status read that fails once at transport level and then succeeds returns the result, the injected sleep was called once with 2000, and the server saw two requests
A transport failure on animateImage rejects after exactly one server request (no retry)
With timeoutMs 50 and a server that never answers, the call rejects with ClippyError message 'timeout' within 500 ms
A tool error (isError) on a read is not retried (one server request)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Approval store: propose and consume tokens
userStories.description: As an owner, I want single-use, expiring approval tokens so that nothing is generated without a click.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 5.4 and 4.3, server/store/film-store.ts and server/env.ts (DATA_DIR; the store reuses the same base: <DATA_DIR>/films/<filmId>).

Create server/generate/approval.ts exporting class ApprovalError extends Error { code: 'bad_token' | 'token_expired' | 'token_used' }, the branded type ConsumedApproval { filmId; sceneId; attempt; consumedAt } (only consume() can create one; use a unique-symbol brand) and createApprovalStore({ dir?: (filmId: string) => string (default: <env.DATA_DIR>/films/<filmId>), now?: () => Date, ttlMs?: number, random?: () => string }).

The store persists data to <dir(filmId)>/approvals.json (write a temp file then rename). Methods: propose(filmId, sceneId, estCredits): { token; attempt; expiresAt } (reuses an unexpired, unconsumed proposal for that scene; otherwise a new 32-hex-character token from crypto.randomBytes(16), expiry now + 30 minutes); consume(token, filmId, sceneId): ConsumedApproval (atomically sets consumedAt before returning; throws ApprovalError); attemptFor(filmId, sceneId): number (1 + the number of consumed approvals for the scene); hasProposal(filmId, sceneId): boolean.
Create server/generate/approval.test.ts with a temp directory and an injected clock.
acceptanceCriteria: propose twice within 30 minutes returns the same token; after 31 minutes it returns a different token; tokens match /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/
consume succeeds once; a second consume throws code 'token_used'; a token for another scene or an unknown token throws 'bad_token'; an expired token throws 'token_expired'
attemptFor is 1 before any consume and 3 after two consumed approvals for the scene; a new store instance on the same directory sees the consumed state
The proposal reuse rule does not return a consumed token (a new propose after a consume returns a new token with attempt incremented)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Guard: the only path to animateImage
userStories.description: As an owner, I want a structural guarantee that nothing can be submitted without a consumed approval so that no credits are spent by accident.

Create server/generate/guard.ts exporting idempotencyKeyFor(filmId, sceneId, attempt): string (join with ':'; replace characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._:-] with '_'; if the result is shorter than 8 characters append ':s7'; always <= 200 characters) and submitApproved(client: ClippyClient, approval: ConsumedApproval, args: AnimateImageArgs): Promise<SubmitResult> which validates args with animateImageArgsSchema, requires args.idempotencyKey === idempotencyKeyFor(approval.filmId, approval.sceneId, approval.attempt) (otherwise throws an Error naming both keys) and then calls client.animateImage(args).

idempotencyKeyFor('film 1', 's/2', 1) returns 'film_1:s_2:1'; idempotencyKeyFor('f', 's', 1) returns 'f:s:1:s7' (8 characters)
The source-scanning test passes on the repository and fails when a temporary file under server/generate/ containing `client.animateImage(x)` is added during the test

userStories.title: Clip request builder
userStories.description: As a server developer, I want a pure builder that turns a scene into valid animate_image arguments so that every request obeys the 10 s rule and the prompt limits.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 5.1 (rules, template and heuristics) and 4.1, server/clippy/types.ts, server/generate/guard.ts and shared/storyboard.ts (Scene.camera).

Create server/generate/request.ts exporting wantsSound(intent): boolean (true when the intent contains pour, splash, sizzle, crackle, fizz, steam, simmer or sound, case-insensitive, as whole words or word starts), snapOmniSeconds(sec): 5.875 | 8 (the smallest of [5.875, 8] that is >= sec, else 8), clipSecondsFor(model, sceneSec): number (fast-h3: round to 1 decimal then clamp to [5.2, 10]; omni: snapOmniSeconds), buildClipPrompt({ intent, camera, adjust?, omni? }): string and buildAnimateRequest({ filmId, aspect, scene: { id, durationSec, intent, camera }, stillUrl, productPhotoUrl?, attempt, adjust?, withSound? }): AnimateImageArgs.

buildClipPrompt follows the template in the design (intent, camera phrase, product-fidelity sentence, 'No text, no logos, no extra products.', optional retry sentence); for fast-h3 trim to 800 characters at a sentence boundary (never mid-word; the result ends with '.', '!' or '?'); omni adds 'Ambient sound only, no speech, no music.' and names <Picture 1> as the scene and <Picture 2> as the product, with a 1200 character cap.

buildAnimateRequest picks model omni when withSound (default wantsSound(intent)), uses idempotencyKeyFor, sets sourceImageUrl for fast-h3 or imageUrls [stillUrl, productPhotoUrl?] for omni, and validates the result with animateImageArgsSchema (a ZodError propagates).
Create server/generate/request.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: clipSecondsFor('fast-h3', 3) is 5.2, ('fast-h3', 12) is 10, ('fast-h3', 7.04) is 7; ('fast-h3-omni', 6) is 8, ('fast-h3-omni', 4) is 5.875, ('fast-h3-omni', 8) is 8

buildClipPrompt with a 2000-character intent returns at most 800 characters, ends with a sentence-ending character and is a prefix-cut at a sentence boundary (no partial word); with adjust true it contains 'Keep the product clearly visible in frame for the whole clip'

buildAnimateRequest for a 9:16 film with intent 'coffee pours into a cup' and stillUrl 'https://app.example.test/api/assets/a1' returns model 'fast-h3-omni', aspect '9:16', imageUrls starting with that URL, durationSec 8 for a 7 s scene, and idempotencyKey 'film1:s2:1' for attempt 1; the same scene with intent 'a slow reveal' returns model 'fast-h3' with sourceImageUrl set
An http:// stillUrl makes buildAnimateRequest throw a ZodError

userStories.description: As a server developer, I want the scene image Clippy will animate chosen from the best available asset and cropped to the film aspect so that clips match the film.

Create server/generate/source-still.ts exporting selectSource(film: FilmState, comp: Comp, sceneId: string): { kind: 'still' | 'flatten' | 'plate' | 'product-photo'; asset?: AssetRef } (order: an asset with role 'still' and that sceneId; else 'flatten' when the scene has bg or product layers with assetIds; else the bg plate asset; else the product photo from film.brief.productAssetId) and prepareSourceStill(ctx: ToolCtx, sceneId: string, aspect: '16:9' | '9:16' | '1:1', flatten?: (...args) => Promise<Buffer>): Promise<{ asset: AssetRef; kind: string }>.

userStories.title: Mode route: flip a scene and get a proposal
userStories.description: As a web client developer, I want POST /scenes/:sceneId/mode so that the user can switch a scene to real video and see exactly what it would cost.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 3, 4.2 and 7, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 5 (the /mode and /approve contract) and section 6 (D-1, D-2, D-4), server/http/handlers/generate.ts (the S2 stub `registerGenerateRoutes(app, deps)`; deps = { films, assets, meta, ledger, bus, makeToolCtx }), server/http/routes.ts (only to see how it is called; never edit it), server/clippy/balance.ts and shared/events.ts.

Create server/generate/types.ts with zod schemas and types for ModeRequest { mode }, Proposal, ModeResponse (the contract's `200 { mode, proposal? }`) and the GenerateErrorCode union from the design section 4.2; create server/generate/services.ts exporting getGenerateServices() (module-level singletons: the approval store, a Clippy client created lazily from env.CLIPPY_MCP_URL and env.CLIPPY_TOKEN or undefined when unset, a balance reader) and setGenerateServicesForTests(services).

Fill server/http/handlers/generate.ts (S2 created it as a 501 stub; S7a owns it): `registerGenerateRoutes(app, deps)` registers POST /api/films/:id/scenes/:sceneId/mode using deps.films and deps.makeToolCtx(filmId). Mode 'motion': commit the change, call the revert handler from the runner registry if one is registered (the registry is created in the next story; import it lazily and tolerate its absence), answer 200 { mode: 'motion' }.

A third generate scene returns 409 { error: 'generate_cap' } and leaves the composition unchanged; an unknown scene returns 404
POST mode 'motion' on a generate scene returns 200 { mode: 'motion' } and meta.director.scenes[scene].mode becomes 'motion'

userStories.description: As a web client developer, I want POST /scenes/:sceneId/approve so that a click starts the clip exactly once.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 3, 5.3, 5.4 and 7, docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 5, server/http/handlers/generate.ts (registerGenerateRoutes from the previous story), server/generate/approval.ts, server/generate/public-url.ts and server/clippy/balance.ts.

Create server/generate/runner-registry.ts exporting type GenerationRunner = { preflight(ctx, sceneId): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; status: number; error: string; retryAfterSec?: number }>; run(ctx, input: { sceneId: string; approval: ConsumedApproval }): Promise<void> }, setGenerationRunner(r), getGenerationRunner(), setRevertHandler(fn) and getRevertHandler() (module-level; S7b registers them).

Extend registerGenerateRoutes in server/http/handlers/generate.ts with POST /api/films/:id/scenes/:sceneId/approve, answering in this order: 404 for an unknown film or scene; 409 { error: 'not_generate_scene' } when the scene is not generate; 501 { error: 'runner_unavailable' } when no runner is registered; 422 { error: 'public_url_invalid', message } when PUBLIC_BASE_URL fails assertPublicUrl; 402 { error: 'insufficient_credits' } when the balance is readable and below 25; the runner's preflight failure status and error (for example 429 rate_limited with retryAfterSec); ONLY THEN consume the token (404 bad_token, 410 token_expired, 409 token_used) and answer 202 { accepted: true } after starting runner.run in the background (never awaited; a rejection emits an error event { where: 'generate', message } and is logged). Errors are always { error: <code> }.
Extend server/http/handlers/generate.test.ts for every status code in that order.
acceptanceCriteria: With a registered fake runner, a valid token returns 202 { accepted: true } and the runner's run is called once with the scene id and a ConsumedApproval; the same token again returns 409 token_used

Failures before the consume leave the token unconsumed: with no runner the response is 501 runner_unavailable, with PUBLIC_BASE_URL 'http://localhost:8787' it is 422 public_url_invalid, with a balance of 10 it is 402 insufficient_credits, with a preflight returning { ok: false, status: 429, error: 'rate_limited', retryAfterSec: 120 } it is 429 and the body has retryAfterSec 120; in each case a later valid request with the same token succeeds
An unknown token returns 404 bad_token and an expired token returns 410 token_expired (injected clock)
A runner whose run rejects does not change the 202 and produces one error event with where 'generate'; server/http/routes.ts is unchanged by this PRD (git diff shows no edit to it)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: useGenerate: state per scene from events
userStories.description: As a UI developer, I want one reducer that turns server events into a per-scene state so that the panel only renders.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 3 (state diagram), 4.2 and 8, shared/events.ts, web/src/api/client.ts and web/src/api/sse.ts.

Create web/src/panels/generate-types.ts mirroring the server's Proposal, ModeResponse and GenerateErrorCode types (plain TypeScript interfaces) and fixtures/s07a/mode-response.json (hand-authored, _handAuthored true); add a test that the fixture parses with the server's ModeResponse zod schema and is assignable to the web ModeResponse type.

Create web/src/panels/useGenerate.ts exporting the pure reduceGenerate(state, event) and the hook useGenerate({ filmId, comp, events, api }): { scenes, review(sceneId), approve(sceneId), keepMotion(sceneId) } where api = { setMode(filmId, sceneId, mode), approve(filmId, sceneId, token) }. Per-scene phases: motion, idle (generate, no proposal), proposed, running, placing, checking, done, failed, needs_retry.

Event mapping: generate.proposed -> proposed (stores the token, reason, estimate); generate.progress statuses approved|submitted|queued|planning|rendering|downloading -> running, placing -> placing, checking -> checking, 'failed: <msg>' and 'timed_out' -> failed with the message, 'cancelled' -> motion; generate.done -> done with the asset and productVisibleFrac; review.finding with kind 'product-missing-in-clip' -> needs_retry until a new generate.proposed arrives. review(sceneId) calls api.setMode(..., 'generate') and stores the returned proposal; approve(sceneId) calls api.approve with the stored token; keepMotion calls api.setMode(..., 'motion').
Create web/src/panels/useGenerate.test.tsx.
acceptanceCriteria: The event sequence proposed, progress rendering, progress downloading, progress placing, progress checking, done (productVisibleFrac 0.92) leaves the scene in phase done with visibleFrac 0.92 and passes through running, placing, checking in order

progress 'failed: pro_plan_required' gives phase failed with that message; progress 'timed_out' gives failed with 'timed out'; a review.finding product-missing-in-clip after done gives needs_retry, and a following generate.proposed gives proposed
approve('s2') calls api.approve once with the token from the stored proposal; with no proposal it does nothing; keepMotion calls api.setMode with 'motion'
The mode-response fixture is assignable to the web type and parses with the server schema
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.description: As an owner, I want a free command that proves my Clippy token and URL work so that I find problems before spending credits.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-07-generate-mode-mcp/design.md sections 9 and 11, scripts/live/run.ts (the dispatcher and the exported shape { describe, estimateUsd, run }) and server/clippy/mcp.ts.

Create scripts/live/s07-connect.ts exporting describe() (what it does; it needs CLIPPY_MCP_URL and CLIPPY_TOKEN; it only reads: list models and credit balance, no job is created, no credit is spent), estimateUsd() returning 0 and run(): create the client, read the models and the balance, time each call, and print summariseConnect(results); throw a clear error naming the missing variable when either is unset.
Export summariseConnect({ models, balance, timings }): string (pure; shows model names, currentBalance and timings; never prints the token or the URL's query).
Create scripts/live/s07-connect.test.ts for the pure parts and the missing-variable error (never contacting a server).

readFirst: docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (types, interfaces, authoring core 4a, helpers and test doubles 4b, HTTP 5, decisions D-1..D-14 in section 6)
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.

No story calls the Clippy MCP server, including in tests: tests use the in-process SDK test server or makeFakeClippy. `animateImage` may only be called from server/clippy/* and server/generate/guard.ts (a test enforces it).
Clippy fixtures are hand-authored and marked "_handAuthored": true; never present them as recorded responses.
S7a never edits server/http/routes.ts (D-1): it fills registerGenerateRoutes in server/http/handlers/generate.ts, which S2 creates as a stub and S7a owns. S7a has no other edit outside its own files.
Never log or return the CLIPPY_TOKEN, a signed resultUrl, or an URL query string.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npm run live -- s07-connect --yes` (free: lists models and the credit balance; no job, no credit) with CLIPPY_MCP_URL and CLIPPY_TOKEN set, and pastes the output (no token) in the PR. It confirms the SDK transport, the bearer header and the balance shape.

MG-2: owner confirms S4 stores the product-in-scene still with role 'still' and sceneId and writes meta.director.productNoun (D-11); S7a falls back to a flatten, the plate or the product photo if not.
MG-3: owner provides PUBLIC_BASE_URL (the S8b deployment or an approved tunnel); without it Approve answers 422 public_url_invalid and nothing is spent.
